title: kv cache: defragmentation, paging & spillover scheduling to reduce memory fragmentation and eviction churn
author: Priya Nair
description: Context: The serving runtime's KV cache was evicting frequently under mixed-length workloads due to memory fragmentation and uncoordinated spillover to host paging. This caused higher tail latency and increased model re-computation for hot prefixes. This PR implements three coordinated changes: (1) background defragmentation to compact scattered KV shards, (2) a paging-aware spillover scheduler that throttles and priorities spill/reload to avoid head-of-line eviction storms, and (3) improved eviction heuristics that consider fragmentation score, recency, and future sequence-length distribution estimated from recent batching. Motivation: lower eviction churn, reduce paging thundering, and improve latency tail at high-utilization. High-level changes: - defragmenter: lightweight background worker that performs in-place compaction on underutilized KV slabs; runs rate-limited and off the critical path. - spillover scheduler: sequence-aware queue that batches spill/restore I/O and prioritizes prefixes with high reuse probability. Uses simple aging heuristic and integrates with autoscaler backpressure signals. - eviction policy: hybrid score = alpha*recency + beta*size-normalized-fragmentation + gamma*predicted-reuse. Tunable via config and defaults chosen from offline/bench results. - instrumentation: new metrics (kv.defrag.runs, kv.fragmentation_score, kv.spill.queue_len, kv.eviction_score_histogram) and tracing spans for spill/restore. - tests & benchmarks: unit tests for allocator invariants, integration test replays with production trace, and perf canary results included. Checklist: - [x] design doc (linked in Linear ENG-6421) - [x] unit tests for allocator and eviction heuristics - [x] integration test with trace replay - [x] perf bench against perf-canary workloads (latency tail reduced ~18% at 90th percentile) - [x] added observability + dashboards - [x] rollout plan (canary -> gradual ramp). Rollout plan: Deploy to canary pool (10% traffic) with defrag disabled by default. Enable defrag and spillover scheduler behind feature flag; monitor kv.fragmentation_score, eviction_rate, latency_p90/p99, and host swap activity. If regressions observed, automatic rollback via route policy after 15m sustained degradation. Backwards compatibility: This change is additive and controlled by feature flags and runtime config; no breaking API changes. Follow-ups: - tune alpha/beta/gamma by customer workload class - add adaptive defrag intensity based on host memory pressure - explore async kernel prefetch hooks to pre-warm KV entries for common long-context patterns
commit_summary: Initial defragmentation worker and slab compaction implementation
Add spillover scheduler with prioritized spill/restore queue and batching
Refactor eviction policy to include fragmentation score and reuse prediction
Add unit & integration tests, metrics, and tracing spans
Perf canary harness updates and benchmark results added
files_changed: runtime/kv_cache/allocator.py (+320 -45) — slab allocator changes, compaction API
runtime/kv_cache/defragmenter.py (+210 -10) — background worker with rate limiter
runtime/kv_cache/eviction_policy.py (+180 -85) — hybrid eviction scoring, fragmentation calc
review_comments: Ethan Chu: Can the defrag worker be scheduled to run only when the host swap/paging is below a threshold? Concern is extra I/O during noisy neighbors.
Priya Nair (author): Added a rate limiter and host-pressure gate; defrag will back off if host.swap_usage > 60% or disk_iops > threshold. See defragmenter.py lines 78-112.
Sasha Ivanov: The fragmentation score calculation looks O(n) over slabs; will this add CPU overhead on hot paths?
Priya Nair: Calculation is amortized — we sample a small set of slabs per interval and maintain rolling averages. Updated the comment and added microbench numbers in the PR description.
Marco Alvarez: Suggest adding an integration alert to the rollout dashboard for spill.queue_len > 50 sustained for 5m — added in the docs.
Ethan Chu: Unit tests look good; can we add a deterministic replay for the eviction policy so we can detect regressions?
Priya Nair: Added tests/integration/test_kv_spill_replay.py which replays a representative production trace and asserts eviction churn <= baseline * 1.05.
merge_outcome: merged (squash) — merged by Marco Alvarez after approvals and green CI; feature flags defaulted off for canary rollout
release_notes:
- runtime: reduce KV cache eviction churn via background defragmentation and spillover scheduling (improves latency tail under high utilization)
- metrics: kv.defrag.runs, kv.fragmentation_score, kv.spill.queue_len were added
- config: runtime.kv.defrag.enabled (false by default), runtime.kv.spill.scheduler.enabled (false by default)
notes_for_ops: Canary steps: 1) Deploy to canary pool with feature flags off. 2) Enable spillover scheduler only and monitor spill.queue_len and eviction_rate for 10m. 3) Enable defrag at low intensity (rate_limit=1 run/min) and monitor kv.defrag.runs and host swap. 4) Gradually increase defrag intensity if stable.
perf_summary: Perf canary against 'kv_fragmentation_workload' shows ~18% p90 latency reduction and ~10% lower avg eviction rate at 85% memory utilization. p99 unchanged in canary; further tuning scheduled in ENG-6555.
additional_context: Related PRs: pr-26843-kv-cache-eviction-fragmentation-paging-spillover.json (previous heuristics), pr-25701-kv-cache-eviction-defragmentation-spillover-optimizations.json.
